data.name: Input
data.data: The ELO guidance asks an agent for "rough, sane sorting": rate new cards {{relative to existing cards in the course||on an absolute 0 to 100 scale}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: In studio mode, an agent's edits reach your files only when you flush, so they {{show up in your diff for review||go straight to production}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Before writing a card, an agent can read the data shape's {{JSON schema||Vue component|database index}}, and `create_card` validates against it.

data.name: Input
data.data: The skuilder MCP server is scoped to {{one course||every course on a server|one learner}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Besides cards, an agent can add structure, such as a prerequisite graph over tags, with the {{create_strategy||tag_card|update_card}} tool.

data.name: Input
data.data:
**Skuilder speaks MCP.** Studio writes a `.mcp.json`, so an agent in your project can read and edit the course you have open.

Its edits reach your files only when you flush, as a reviewable diff.

[Read: Connect Agents](/vue-skuilder/do/mcp.html)

data.name: Input
data.data: To a session, a course is a content source: something that answers `getWeightedCards(limit)` with {{scored candidate cards||a fixed list of card IDs|rendered Vue components}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A card you miss during a session goes to the failed queue, and the session won't end until {{it has been cleared||you review it tomorrow|the next session starts}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Ratings and the review schedule are updated from {{the first attempt||the last attempt|the average of all attempts}} at a card in a presentation.

data.name: Input
data.data: Turning a selected card ID into something renderable (fetch its data, build its question, pick its view) is called {{hydration||compilation|serialization}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: The `SessionController`, the navigation pipeline and the data layer live in `@vue-skuilder/db`, which {{has no Vue dependency||requires a Vue app instance}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: When the supply queue runs low mid-session, the controller {{re-runs the pipeline (a replan)||ends the session early|repeats cards already seen}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: New cards and reviews are drawn from {{one supply queue, in pipeline rank order||separate new and review queues, mixed by a fixed ratio}}.

data.name: Input
data.data:
**The study loop**: show a card, take a response, update the learner model, choose the next card.

`StudySession` (Vue) renders it; `SessionController` (no Vue) drives it. Cards come from one **supply** queue, in pipeline rank order; misses go to a **failed** queue.

[Read: The Big Picture](/vue-skuilder/learn/architecture.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**A card type has three parts:** a **DataShape** (its fields), a **Question** class (grades a response), and **views** (Vue components that render it).

Each card names its view: `{courseware}.question.{Question}.{View}`.

[Read: Card Data Model](/vue-skuilder/learn/card-data-model.html)

data.name: Input
data.data: The platform cares about two moments in a custom card's life: it receives data, and {{it submits an answer||it unmounts|it fetches its own data}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A view that plays an animation after answering can return {{deferAdvance||fluent: false|isCorrect: null}} and emit `ready-to-advance` when it's done.

data.name: Input
data.data: For a custom widget inside otherwise-markdown cards, {{an inline component||a full custom card type}} is the lighter option.

data.name: Input
data.data: The scaffold names its courseware `ExampleCourse`. The time to rename it is {{before authoring real content||after the first deploy|never, since the name is ignored}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A study session finds your views through {{the allCourseWare registry||the Vue router|a global CSS class}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Inside a view, `submitAnswer(answer)` from `useQuestionView` {{grades the answer and hands a record to the session||writes straight to the user's database}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: In the default card syntax, the double bar `||` separates {{correct answers from distractors||one blank from the next|the question from its hint}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: An evaluation with `fluent: false` marks an answer as {{correct but too slow||wrong but close|skipped}}, so the card comes back sooner.

data.name: Input
data.data: A question's correct/incorrect verdict drives {{spaced repetition: extend or reset the interval||the card's rating only|nothing, since only performance matters}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: One data shape can have several views (`7 + 4 = ?`, or "seven plus four?"). Varying the presentation helps avoid {{overfitting a skill to one presentation||duplicate rows in the database}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A question type can ship its own content (say, every sum from 0+0 to 9+9) through {{static seedData||a CSV import|the MCP server}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A spelling card can grade `cat` spelled `kat` as `{ _global: 0.67, c: 0, a: 1, t: 1 }`, so that {{each letter's skill is rated separately||the card is retried three times|the answer is auto-corrected}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A card type has a DataShape (its data schema), a Question (its grading), and {{one or more views (Vue components)||a reducer|a route}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A card's view ID embeds the question class and view component names, so renaming a view component {{breaks existing cards||is harmless, since IDs are random UUIDs}}.

data.name: Input
data.data:
**A custom card is a Vue component that can do anything**: a game, a chess board, a keyboard. The platform cares about two moments: it receives data, and it submits an answer (`submitAnswer`), which your `Question` class grades.

[Read: Creating Custom Cards](/vue-skuilder/extend/custom-cards.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**Everything goes through data-layer interfaces**, with two implementations:

- **couch**: CouchDB + PouchDB. Accounts, sync, live card ratings.
- **static**: JSON from any host; learner data in the browser. This course is static.

[Read: Data Layer](/vue-skuilder/learn/data-layer.html)

data.name: Input
data.data: On CouchDB, a course can opt in to `localSync`, where the app {{copies the course into the browser and reads from the copy||caches only the current session's cards}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A static app's root `skuilder.json` maps course names to URLs, and those URLs {{may point at another site||must be on the same origin}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: In a static deployment, card ratings are {{frozen at pack time||updated from every learner's answers}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Because its strategy documents are packed with it, a static course {{runs the same navigation pipeline as a live one||falls back to random card order}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: With the static data layer, a learner's history, reviews and ratings persist {{in that browser only||across devices, via sync}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Navigation strategies are stored as {{documents in the course database||code in the app bundle only|rows in a config file}}, each naming an implementing class and its config.

data.name: Input
data.data: The data layer's two implementations, chosen by `type` at startup, are {{couch and static||sql and nosql|local and remote}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: This course's questions are held back by a custom filter that reads {{which docs pages you've read||your GitHub activity|the server's access logs}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Because every filter multiplies scores, {{filter order doesn't change the final score||the last filter always wins}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A custom filter is registered at app start, then enabled for a course by {{a strategy document naming it||an entry in package.json|a CSS class on its cards}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A filter and the app can share one source of truth by reading and writing the same {{strategy state document||Vue store|URL parameter}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: If a strategy document names a class the app never registered, the pipeline {{skips it with a warning||refuses to start the session}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A filter that scores a card 0 {{excludes it from the run||sends it to the failed queue}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: The diversity re-rank demotes a card whose distinctive tags {{already appear among higher-ranked cards||are unknown to the course}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Review due dates mean {{eligible||overdue}}: the system keeps a healthy backlog of reviews rather than racing it to zero.

data.name: Input
data.data: Scoring is gain-based, so a correct but slow answer {{gains less||lowers the learner's rating}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: A filter that means "not ready yet", such as a prerequisite check, is a {{gate||signal}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: In the navigation pipeline, {{generators||filters|regulators}} propose candidate cards; filters then multiply their scores.

data.name: Input
data.data: Pressure for new material can lift new cards, but only those {{no gate held back||with the highest ratings|the learner has seen before}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Evolutionary orchestration (tuning strategy weights from learner outcomes) is currently {{partly wired: weights vary, but outcomes aren't recorded yet||fully running in production}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: Each selected card carries provenance: {{a record of what each stage did to its score, and why||its author and edit history|the URL it was loaded from}}.

data.name: Input
data.data: The skill pressure filter boosts cards on a learner's {{weakest or least settled skills||most recently practiced skills|highest-rated skills}}.

data.name: Input
data.data:
**How the next card is chosen:** a pipeline. **Generators** propose candidates; **filters** multiply their scores (a *gate* says "not yet", a *signal* says "prefer"); the best are selected.

Each card carries **provenance**: what every stage did, and why.

[Read: Pedagogy](/vue-skuilder/learn/pedagogy.html)

Questions about a docs page unlock once you've read that page, or met its intro card here.

data.data:
**The static-course workflow:** `cli init` a course, `npm run studio` to edit it locally, **flush** to write it back to your files, then build and deploy anywhere static.
